steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Polyrhythm (multiple conflicting rhythmic patterns simultaneously) is central to African music — it creates complex, layered rhythmic textures.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Caribbean genres each have distinct rhythmic signatures: reggae (off-beat skank guitar, one-drop drumming), ska (fast off-beat), calypso (syncopated melody).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cyclic structures repeat musical patterns — unlike Western through-composed forms, African music often builds intensity through cyclical repetition and layering.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Afrobeat (Fela Kuti) combines West African highlife with jazz, funk and Yoruba music — it demonstrates how fusion creates entirely new genres.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
